SUBJECT:
fix(web): resolve the Claude SDK from the host, never from the task worktree
BODY:
Security review finding: the Claude sidecar ran with the task worktree as its
working directory and resolved the SDK itself, so a repository could get its
own code loaded.

- the bare package import resolved from the worktree, so a repo-supplied
  node_modules/@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk would have been imported and run
  inside the Ajax server
- `npm root -g` ran inside the worktree, where a project .npmrc can redirect the
  global root to an attacker-chosen directory

The host now runs `npm root -g` from the home directory, picks the direct
global SDK path (falling back to the copy nested under the old claude-agent-acp
bridge), and passes the absolute path as --sdk-module. The sidecar loads only
that module: no package import, no npm, no child_process; with no --sdk-module
it refuses to initialise. A missing SDK fails the spawn with an error that
names the install command.

- tests: path picker (direct, nested only, both, none) against static fixture
  roots; the sidecar refuses to resolve anything itself; a source check that
  the forbidden strings are gone
- docs: the Claude section describes host-side resolution
